item.title: Rouge trader poster., 27th July
item.description:
A grey truck was recently seen in the Boevey Path area, with the driver operating a drone over and close to residential properties. The operator appeared to be controlling the drone from inside the vehicle, raising concerns about whether they maintained a clear, direct line of sight. When approached and questioned, the driver became hostile. The following day, an advertisement for “All Season Roofing and Building” was attached to a nearby lamp post. The business does not appear to be registered as a limited company, and the timing has caused concern that the drone may have been used to inspect or identify roofs before approaching local residents. There are known scams where traders claim to have noticed roof damage while working nearby, target elderly or vulnerable residents, and then use high-pressure sales tactics. In some cases, they may initially offer a minor repair but later claim that extensive and expensive work is required. Please could the council investigate the unauthorised advertising, identify the business or vehicle involved, and consider whether Trading Standards or the relevant drone enforcement authority should be informed. Local residents may also benefit from a warning not to agree to unsolicited roofing work without obtaining independent quotations and checking the trader’s credentials.

Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): Croft Close, Upper Belvedere, Greater London
Report on FixMyStreet
